title: Daily AI & Tech News Brief
summary: Concise AI, mobile, consumer-device, cybersecurity, and open-source technology news summaries with source links.

items.title: OpenAI previews GPT-5.6 Sol with tighter cyber-safety controls
items.summary: OpenAI previewed GPT-5.6 Sol, a next-generation model aimed at stronger coding, science, and cybersecurity work. Access is restricted during the preview and paired with stronger safeguards for sensitive cyber capabilities.

items.title: Asian AI labs pitch Mythos-like models amid U.S. export limits
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Sakana AI's Fugu and 360's Tulongfeng are being positioned as alternatives to Anthropic models restricted by U.S. export controls. The story highlights how model access limits are shaping regional AI competition.

items.title: Qwen posts Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B on Hugging Face
items.summary: Qwen's Hugging Face organization now lists Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B. It is an undated model-listing signal rather than a full launch article, but it is relevant for tracking agent-focused open model releases.

items.title: DeepSeek lists DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark on Hugging Face
items.summary: DeepSeek's Hugging Face organization now lists DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark. Because the listing is undated, treat it as a model-tracking signal rather than a confirmed timed launch announcement.

items.title: Google Finance exits beta with a new Android app
items.summary: Google is moving its upgraded Google Finance experience out of beta and launching a dedicated Android app. The update is a practical consumer-platform change for market tracking on phones.

items.title: GRC-agent walkthrough shows practical AI automation for security teams
items.summary: A BleepingComputer walkthrough explains how a GRC agent can monitor controls, spot evidence gaps, and open remediation tasks. It is a useful example of AI agents moving into repetitive security and compliance workflows.

items.title: OpenAI previews GPT-5.6 Sol for limited enterprise testing
items.summary: OpenAI previewed GPT-5.6 Sol, describing stronger coding, science, and cybersecurity capabilities with an upgraded safety stack. Axios reports the broader GPT-5.6 preview is limited to about 20 companies and disclosed to the U.S. government.

items.title: Google Finance gets a refreshed app and wider rollout
items.summary: Google is moving its upgraded Google Finance experience out of beta and launching a new Android app, adding practical market-tracking features for everyday users.

items.title: Hugging Face highlights hybrid-model token prediction research
items.summary: Hugging Face published AllenAI research on which tokens hybrid models predict better, a useful technical look at model behavior and evaluation for AI builders.

items.title: GRC agents show how AI can reduce repetitive compliance work
items.summary: A BleepingComputer walkthrough explains how an AI agent can continuously monitor controls, identify evidence gaps, and open remediation tasks for governance, risk, and compliance teams.

items.title: Chinese-speaking APT uses new TinyRCT backdoor in Southeast Asia
items.summary: The Hacker News reports that a Chinese-speaking threat actor is deploying a custom TinyRCT backdoor against government entities and critical infrastructure targets in Southeast Asia.

items.title: OSI announces an Open Source AI Fellowship at UN Open Source Week
items.summary: The Open Source Initiative announced an Open Source AI Fellowship connected to UN Open Source Week, extending public work on open AI governance and collaboration.

items.title: Google Finance exits beta and adds a new Android app
items.summary: Google is rolling out an upgraded Google Finance experience, including a dedicated Android app and new market-tracking features for everyday investors.

items.title: OpenAI and Broadcom introduce an LLM inference chip
items.summary: OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled Jalapeño, a custom chip aimed at making large-language-model inference faster and more efficient at scale.

items.title: New macOS malware tries to mislead AI analysis tools
items.summary: Researchers found macOS malware that embeds fake errors and prompt-injection-style strings to confuse AI-assisted malware analysis workflows.

items.title: Popular Chrome ad blocker carried dormant script-injection capability
items.summary: A YouTube ad-blocking Chrome extension with more than 10 million installs was found to include code capable of injecting arbitrary JavaScript.

items.title: OSI launches an Open Source AI Fellowship at UN Open Source Week
items.summary: The Open Source Initiative announced a fellowship focused on open source AI, tying AI governance and open collaboration into UN Open Source Week.

items.title: Google Research details linear elastic caching for cloud economics
items.summary: Google Research published work on linear elastic caching, an approach intended to improve cloud efficiency and economics for large-scale services.

items.title: OpenAI and Broadcom unveil an LLM inference chip
items.summary: OpenAI and Broadcom announced Jalapeño, a custom chip designed for large-language-model inference. The goal is better performance, efficiency, and scale for production AI systems.

items.title: Google Research studies how reasoning improves LLM recall
items.summary: Google Research published work on how reasoning steps can unlock parametric knowledge in large language models, pointing to better ways to evaluate and prompt models when answers are already inside their weights.

items.title: Hugging Face shows NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel fine-tuning workflows
items.summary: Hugging Face published a guide to accelerating Transformer fine-tuning with NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel, useful for developers building or adapting models with more efficient training workflows.

items.title: Runlayer raises $30M to build infrastructure for enterprise AI agents
items.summary: Runlayer raised a $30 million Series A led by Felicis for its infrastructure and control layer for enterprise AI agents, bringing its total funding to $42 million.

items.title: Windows 11 preview update adds Point-in-Time restore
items.summary: Microsoft's Windows 11 KB5095093 preview update starts rolling out a Point-in-Time restore feature and fixes multiple bugs, giving PC users another recovery option after system problems.

items.title: Fake AI agent skill reportedly passed scanners and reached 26,000 agents
items.summary: The Hacker News reports that security firm AIR placed a fake AI-agent skill through marketplace and ad channels, where tested scanners marked it safe and it reportedly reached about 26,000 agents.

items.title: OSI announces an Open Source AI Fellowship
items.summary: The Open Source Initiative announced an Open Source AI Fellowship at UN Open Source Week, extending its work on open AI definitions, policy, and community governance.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Tag as a Slack-native AI coworker
items.summary: Anthropic introduced Claude Tag, a beta agentic assistant for Claude Team and Enterprise customers that works inside Slack, learns workspace context, and can suggest or coordinate follow-up work.

items.title: OpenAI says GPT-5 Pro helped solve a long-running immunology mystery
items.summary: OpenAI published a case study describing how GPT-5 Pro helped immunologist Derya Unutmaz reason through a three-year T cell research problem, pointing to possible uses in cancer and autoimmune research workflows.

items.title: Hugging Face and IBM Research show CUGA examples for agentic apps
items.summary: A new Hugging Face post from IBM Research demonstrates CUGA with two dozen working examples for building agentic applications on a lightweight harness, useful for developers evaluating practical agent patterns.

items.title: OSI announces an Open Source AI Fellowship at UN Open Source Week
items.summary: The Open Source Initiative announced an Open Source AI Fellowship during UN Open Source Week, extending its work around open AI definitions, policy, and community governance.

items.title: Fake AI agent skill reportedly passed security scans and reached 26,000 agents
items.summary: The Hacker News reports that security firm AIR placed a fake AI-agent skill through marketplace and ad channels, where it allegedly passed tested scanners and reached about 26,000 agents, highlighting supply-chain risks for agent ecosystems.

items.title: Microsoft fixes AutoGen Studio flaw that could enable code execution
items.summary: Microsoft patched an AutoGen Studio vulnerability chain nicknamed AutoJack that could let a malicious webpage manipulate an AI agent into running commands on its host system.

items.title: Scattered Spider hackers plead guilty in UK Transport for London case
items.summary: KrebsOnSecurity reports that two men linked to the Scattered Spider cybercrime group pleaded guilty on the first day of trial over the 2024 attack that disrupted Transport for London.

items.title: OpenAI launches Patch the Planet for open-source security fixes
items.summary: OpenAI announced Patch the Planet, a Daybreak initiative that will help open-source maintainers find, validate, and fix security vulnerabilities using AI plus expert review. The program is notable because it connects agentic AI work with practical software-supply-chain security.

items.title: Microsoft fixes AutoGen Studio flaw that allowed command execution
items.summary: BleepingComputer reports that Microsoft fixed an AutoGen Studio vulnerability chain called AutoJack. The issue could let a malicious webpage manipulate an AI agent workflow into running commands on the host, underlining why agent tooling needs strong sandboxing and prompt-boundary defenses.

items.title: Canada used a first-of-its-kind warrant to clean botnet-infected devices
items.summary: The Hacker News says Canada's spy agency received court authorization to neutralize two foreign-run botnets on infected servers, routers, and IoT devices located in Canada. The case is important because it shows a more active legal model for disrupting compromised infrastructure.

items.title: Hugging Face highlights PP-OCRv6 for multilingual OCR
items.summary: Hugging Face published a post on PP-OCRv6, a family of OCR models covering 50 languages with sizes from 1.5M to 34.5M parameters. It is useful for developers who need document, image-text, or creator-tool pipelines that can run with smaller OCR models.

items.title: Qwen posts a Qwen Image Bench repository on Hugging Face
items.summary: Qwen's Hugging Face organization now lists Qwen-Image-Bench, a repository related to image benchmarking. It is a model-listing signal rather than a full launch post, but it is relevant for tracking Qwen's multimodal evaluation ecosystem.
